accuracy.evidence: Checked against the English National Curriculum (2014) Appendix 2, Year 2 'expanded noun phrases for description and specification' (the blue butterfly, plain flour, the man in the moon) and the Year 2 pupil terminology (noun, noun phrase, adjective, comma); determiner is correctly placed in Year 4. Commas are only taught between coordinate adjectives (the old, creaky door) and the adult text notes the size-before-colour order needs no comma (big black dog). CCSS L.1.1f and L.2.1f cited for US families.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the known Year 2 slips: adjective after the noun (Word order prediction 'the cat fluffy', m3, sorter card 'cat fluffy the'), counting a verb as part of the phrase (sleeps/jumps tiles in Which one?, 'hid.' in Find the phrase, m6, m8 'the dog runs'), a comma after the article or before the noun (comma gaps 1 and 3, p3), and vague words that pick out nothing (Best word prediction nice vs enormous, m2).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagnph is a grammar lab: each describing word dropped onto 'the cat' filters a line-up of four drawn cats, hats or balls until only the starred one is left, so specification is seen, not told. Then ordered slots, comma gaps and a tap-every-word phrase finder. flagdesc (Describing aloud) is speaking and listening with senses and voice volume; flagnv sorts nouns and verbs. Shingle gate: highest similarity 5.2% (flagsorry), 4.8% (flagfriend).

lab_teaches.evidence: Adding 'small' leaves two cats standing, adding 'ginger' leaves one, so the child discovers that each adjective rules things out. A wrong adjective names the clash ('The big cat? Look at the star. It is small.'), a verb tile is rejected as a doing word. In Word order, tapping the noun first gives 'cat is the noun, the thing. It goes last.' The comma step only accepts the gap between the two describing words.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions: where the describing word goes (tempting 'after the noun: the cat fluffy'), where the comma goes, and whether 'a nice dog' or 'an enormous dog' helps more. Each is tested by the next task and the done line quotes the child's guess through A.reveal.

challenge_feedback.evidence: The challenge rotates expanded-noun-phrase questions and hint() returns a specific m= message for each wrong choice: a doing word makes it a sentence, the noun must go last, a comma after 'the' is not needed, a vague word does not help the reader picture it. Wrong taps inside every step are also named in the canvas aria-label and the say line.

readability.evidence: Kid text FK 0.8 against the family target 5.0, in short sentences with concrete nouns (cat, hat, door). Adult text FK 6.7 against 10.0 and uses the precise terms: head noun, modifiers, determiner, expanded noun phrase, description and specification, coordinate adjectives.

no_filler.evidence: Filler and overlap gates passed. Kid paragraphs cover noun phrase, expanding it, order, and commas plus precise word choice; adult paragraphs give the curriculum statement and terms, the grammar of head noun and modifiers, five named mistakes, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark for all six steps, before and after Show me: the four-cat line-up and star sit above a wide phrase box and two rows of large word tiles; ordered slots and comma gaps fit at 390 px; the challenge cat now sits above its phrase after a fix for text overlapping the drawing. phone_sweep for lesson 406 reported 0 findings.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs (gate_browser) passed on desktop and iPhone 13: every Show me task completed, challenge reached, axe clean in both themes, no console errors. Every drag has a button twin (word buttons under the canvas), and a desktop drag test confirmed 'sleeps' is rejected and 'small' + 'ginger' completes the round with the aria-label updated.
